What this view means

Drag to pan; use the wheel or + / − to zoom. Click inside the boundary to see all four values and the number of clear Sentinel observations.

All measures at a glance

NDVI: Vegetation greenness. Higher values generally mean denser, greener vegetation; values near zero often indicate bare or built surfaces, and negative values can indicate water or shadow.

NDWI: Surface-water contrast using green and near-infrared light. Higher values often indicate open water; lower values commonly indicate vegetation or built ground. Near-zero values are ambiguous.

NDMI: Vegetation moisture proxy. Higher values generally indicate more water in vegetation; lower values can indicate drier vegetation or non-vegetated surfaces. It is not a direct measurement of soil moisture.

LST: Land-surface temperature in °C. Higher values mean a warmer observed surface, not warmer air; differences can also reflect acquisition time, weather and surface material.

NDVI, NDWI and NDMI usually range from −1 to +1. The legend shows this map’s display range, not universal category thresholds. Interpret values in context.

Data and method

Indices: the arithmetic mean of up to 10 selected Sentinel-2 L2A observations, one least-cloudy tile per month, with cloud, shadow and defective pixels excluded using SCL. Pixel counts differ. March and June contributed no clear campus pixels; September contributed clear pixels on 2.5% of the campus grid. Means are not based on every available acquisition.

NDVI = (B08 − B04)/(B08 + B04); NDWI = (B03 − B08)/(B03 + B08); NDMI = (B08 − B11)/(B08 + B11). B03, B04 and B08 are 10 m; B11 and SCL are 20 m, resampled nearest to the 10 m grid. Display interpolation does not add detail.

LST: existing 30 m Landsat Collection 2 surface-temperature raster, one selected scene per month and quality masked, °C. This is not Sentinel temperature, and is not air temperature. The last selected October scene is 6 October. October remains incomplete as of 28 October.

Campus boundary: project layer UPOU Boundary. Orthomosaic: project September 2026 aligned, shadow-reduced image. Transparent gaps mean no usable raster value. Edge cells are selected by pixel centre and clipped to the boundary for display.

Source: Copernicus Sentinel data via Earth Search; free Copernicus licence. LST: USGS Landsat, existing project layer. Orthomosaic: user-provided.
